name: Rankovićism
summary: Rankovićism is the label for the views of Aleksandar Ranković, Tito's security chief and long-time deputy: a centralist, party-orthodox communism that opposed devolving power to the Yugoslav republics and the market-oriented reforms of the mid-1960s. It relied on a powerful security service and favoured Serb and Montenegrin dominance in Kosovo. After his removal in 1966 the term became a pejorative for centralism, police rule and Serb hegemony.
scope: The political line associated with Ranković in the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, roughly 1945 to 1966, as described in Wikipedia's articles on Rankovićism and Ranković, the 1966 Executive Committee minutes on his fall and Bešlin's essay. Ranković wrote little theory, so the profile rests on documented policy and on charges and scholarship about him; answers on issues outside Yugoslav communist politics are mostly inferred and low confidence. It excludes later Serbian nationalism that invoked his name.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Yugoslav communist officials of the period treated health care as a state-provided social service; nothing in the sources suggests Ranković's circle opposed it.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wages were set administratively in a socialist economy and the sources record no Ranković position on minimum wages, so an adherent is neutral.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Bešlin places Ranković against the 1965 market-oriented reform, so a Rankovićist distrusts the claim that markets beat state direction.

public-ownership.rationale: He was a committed communist official in a state-owned economy and favoured the centralised Soviet-style system, so public ownership of core industry is assumed.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from his communist egalitarian commitments; private wealth was already marginal, and no source gives a specific tax stance.

unions-good.rationale: Unions in his Yugoslavia were party-led transmission belts; an adherent would back them as party instruments but not as independent bodies, so the answer is split.

property-fundamental.rationale: A communist official overseeing a socialist state would hold that private property yields to socialist ownership and state needs.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Inferred: few private corporations existed, and a centralist party-state would favour tight state control over any enterprise.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inferred from communist social-policy commitments; the sources do not discuss welfare cuts.

worker-ownership.rationale: Self-management was official Yugoslav doctrine but Bešlin presents Ranković as orthodox and centralist; whether he backed collective worker ownership is not documented.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Ranković built OZNA and led the UDBA, which reportedly spied even on the party leadership; the 1966 Executive Committee minutes charge only that it escaped party control, not that surveillance itself was wrong.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from a conservative, order-minded security chief; drugs are not discussed in the sources.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Tito-era law punished nationalist speech, but Ranković was accused of shielding Serb chauvinism himself, so an adherent is genuinely split.

strong-leader.rationale: He was a loyal associate of Tito, whose strong personal leadership he served, though he himself was charged with building a rival power base.

state-harmful.rationale: He built and ran the repressive state apparatus and favoured centralism; the state's necessity is beyond question for him.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred from a security chief wanting a state monopoly of force; no source addresses civilian gun ownership.

empower-police-military.rationale: His career is defined by building and commanding the security services (OZNA, then UDBA) and by the police-state rule of the 'Ranković era' in Kosovo.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from conservative communist-era morality; sources are silent.

decide-locally.rationale: Wikipedia's account of Rankovićism names centralism as its core: he opposed devolving power to the republics as a threat to Yugoslav and Serb unity.

rehabilitation.rationale: Inferred from his repressive policing and purges after 1948; sources do not discuss penal philosophy.

traditional-family.rationale: Inferred from conventional communist social conservatism of the 1950s-60s; not documented.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred from the era and his orthodox outlook; homosexuality was criminal in Serbia in his time.

abortion-legal.rationale: Yugoslav communists liberalised abortion progressively; his own view is undocumented, so inferred as split.

more-religion-public.rationale: The Kosovo account records Islam being repressed under his security regime, and communists kept religion out of public life.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Inferred: his Kosovo policy favoured Serb and Montenegrin dominance over Albanians, the opposite of correcting group inequities.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed anywhere in the sources; Marxist orthodoxy of his time did not frame gender this way.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Serbs saw him as a defender of Serb interests, but as a communist he officially backed Yugoslav rather than ethnic culture, so the answer is a weak yes.

gradual-change.rationale: He was a conservative upholder of established party order, yet his own career was built on revolution and purges, so adherents are split.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration was not a live issue in socialist Yugoslavia and the sources say nothing.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Inferred from a centralist who guarded state sovereignty and distrusted outside influence; undocumented.

free-trade.rationale: Bešlin ties him to opposition to the market-liberalising 1965 reform, so free trade is inferred as disfavoured.

nation-first.rationale: Inferred from his suspicion of foreign influence and Yugoslav sovereignty; no source states it directly.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Inferred from Yugoslav non-interventionist state doctrine; undocumented for him.

open-borders.rationale: Inferred: a security chief of a closed communist state; borders were tightly policed.

limit-growth.rationale: Inferred from communist commitment to industrialisation; the issue did not arise.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate policy did not exist as an issue in his time, and nothing in the sources lets one infer a position, so neutral.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Inferred from standard communist faith in industrial modernisation.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic issue not addressed in the sources.

revolution-justified.rationale: A Partisan leader who founded the revolutionary security service, but his later stance was defending the established order, so only a moderate yes.

experts-over-public.rationale: Not documented; party-guided rule rather than expert or popular rule.

central-planning.rationale: The Wikipedia article states he supported a centralised, Soviet-style system, which implies backing central direction of the economy.

socialized-markets.rationale: He opposed the market reform of 1965 that moved Yugoslavia toward market socialism, so he is sceptical.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed; no information in the sources.

basic-income.rationale: Inferred from orthodox socialist work-based distribution; not discussed.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: A centralist state-planner opposed to market liberalisation would favour protected state industry; inferred.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Central direction of investment follows from the centralised Soviet-style system he supported.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Inferred: a communist favouring state and social ownership over wide small ownership.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Orthodox communist aim in the distant future but not discussed by him or by sources; split.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: A centralist who backed state direction of the economy would not leave money to the market; this is inferred, not documented.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Inferred: party-state rather than corporatist bodies set wages in his system.

one-party-rule.rationale: He was a leading official of the League of Communists and purged rivals; his removal was charged as a factional power struggle inside the single party, never as a challenge to one-party rule.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: He was a Partisan communist leader and Yugoslavia was a republic after the monarchy was overthrown.

democracy-best.rationale: He operated a one-party police state and favoured centralism; multiparty democracy was not his model.

direct-votes.rationale: Inferred from his centralist, party-led outlook.

workers-councils.rationale: Bešlin portrays him as orthodox and closer to Stalinist control than to reformist self-management, so he is wary of councils as the basis of power.

right-to-secede.rationale: He opposed decentralising power to the republics as a threat to Yugoslav unity, so a right to secede would contradict his position.

natural-rulers.rationale: Not addressed; party elites ruled by ideology rather than by nature.

political-violence-never.rationale: He created the Partisan-era security service OZNA, ran purges after 1948, and policed Kosovo with force.

war-builds-character.rationale: Not documented; Partisan veteran but no stated view.

separate-church-state.rationale: Communist Yugoslavia separated the two, and the Kosovo account has his regime repressing Islam.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: A communist who repressed Islam in Kosovo would reject scripture-based law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: He built the state security apparatus and favoured the state monopoly of force.

military-superiority.rationale: Inferred from a security-minded Partisan leader; not documented.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Officially he stood for a multinational Yugoslavia, though his Kosovo policy favoured Serb dominance, so a mild rejection.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Marxist orthodoxy of the League of Communists, which he held as a party loyalist.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Undocumented; communist egalitarian rhetoric against actual privilege in the nomenklatura.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: His Kosovo policy treated Albanian claims to autonomy as a security threat, so granting group authority over land runs against it.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Reparations for colonialism are not discussed in any source about him or his circle, so neutral.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred from a Yugoslav-communist outlook rather than religious or civilizational unions.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Communist ethics favoured collective duty over individual self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: A party-state security chief who prioritised order and loyalty over individual rights.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental philosophy is outside anything recorded about him; no basis to place him either way.

limit-population.rationale: Population policy is not discussed in the sources on Ranković, so no position can be shown.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Inferred from communist faith in industrialisation.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Not documented; orthodox conservative on institutions.

human-enhancement.rationale: Human enhancement is an anachronistic issue with no basis in the sources, so neutral.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from preference for party control.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: The security chief oversaw wiretapping and bugging of the leadership, so state-proof communication is opposed.

restore-past-order.rationale: Bešlin calls him conservative about party order, but he is a revolutionary-born communist, not a restorationist.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Described as dogmatic and orthodox, so an adherent puts ideology first.

direct-action.rationale: After the revolution he defended party and state institutions rather than street politics.

means-match-ends.rationale: His own methods, purges and police surveillance, were not meant to mirror the society he wanted.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Any Marxist committed to industrial socialism, as he was, would reject a return to hunter-gathering.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Marxist aim in the abstract but not documented for him.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Orthodox communist ultimate aim; no documented view, so neutral.

production-for-use.rationale: Planned socialist production for social needs is the Soviet-style system he backed.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Standard Marxist-Leninist teaching, which he held as a party official.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: He helped run the Yugoslav party-state and its purges after 1948, a Leninist practice of rule.

collective-farming.rationale: Yugoslavia abandoned forced collectivisation in the early 1950s; his own view is undocumented.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Marxist-Leninist teaching he would have professed; undocumented.

taxation-theft.rationale: A state-socialist official would reject this.

harm-principle.rationale: His security regime restricted adults far beyond harm to others.

individual-rights-only.rationale: His policy treated people by national group, privileging Serbs and Montenegrins in Kosovo, and subordinated individuals to the party.

conscription.rationale: A Partisan commander and security chief who favoured a strong army.

exit-over-voice.rationale: His regime pressed Albanians and Muslims to emigrate but denied political voice; the claim that exit beats voting is foreign to a party-state.

state-as-business.rationale: A communist state official would reject this model.

positive-liberty.rationale: Marxist outlook gives some support, but undocumented for him.

media-academia-power.rationale: The sources do not discuss universities and media as power centres, so he is left neutral.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Officially communist Yugoslavia rejected racial science.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation through families and trade bodies conflicts with the party-led centralism he defended; inferred.

total-state.rationale: His party-state and secret police reached into many areas of life, but no stated doctrine of total direction of culture.

national-rebirth.rationale: Not a fascist or revivalist outlook; defender of the existing communist order.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Yugoslav communist policy was defending its borders, not expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Rule by party institutions, though personal loyalty to Tito mattered in practice.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom is incompatible with communist ideology and with every position attributed to him.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Epistemology of this kind is not discussed in the sources on him, so neutral at low confidence.

universal-morality.rationale: Marxist relativism about morality versus universalism; undocumented.

single-common-good.rationale: Party-led socialism assumes a single collective interest, inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Zionism and Israel are not discussed in the sources on Ranković, so no stance can be shown.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora return rights are not addressed in any source about him.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed; Yugoslav language policy favoured a common state language.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Bešlin portrays him as opposed to the reformist and self-management direction.

school-vouchers.rationale: Communist state education; no private choice.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal stimulus theory does not apply to a planned economy and no source records his view.

economic-freedom.rationale: He opposed economic liberalisation and defended party control.

rule-by-example.rationale: His rule rested on police and party power, not moral example.

national-self-determination.rationale: His policy denied Albanians self-rule and insisted on Yugoslav unity, though Serbs saw him as a defender of Serb interests.

force-without-un.rationale: Use of force abroad without the UN is not addressed in the sources about him.

reason-over-faith.rationale: As an orthodox Marxist he is rationalist and anti-religious, but the statement's absolute wording and lack of sources keep this inferred.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Welfare for immigrants was not an issue in socialist Yugoslavia and no source gives his view.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Inferred from the socialist duty to work; undocumented.

class-collaboration.rationale: Marxist-Leninist rejection of class collaboration in principle.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Inferred; no sign of an iconoclastic outlook.

dominated-front.rationale: Not addressed; Yugoslavia took a non-aligned path.

workers-nation.rationale: Officially he was an internationalist communist, though his own practice favoured Serb interests.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Official equality of the sexes versus conventional views; undocumented.

ban-interest.rationale: A ban on interest is not discussed in the sources on his economic outlook.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Contrary to the official ideology of Yugoslav communism.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxist-Leninist theory held by party officials.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred from the priority his industrialising state gave to heavy industry and energy output.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Immigration was not an issue in his setting and no source gives a view.

elite-replacement.rationale: The replacement conspiracy theory has no place in his worldview or in anything recorded about him.

proportional-representation.rationale: His single-party system had no competing parties, so proportional seat allocation does not fit; inferred.

national-mission.rationale: Official Yugoslav policy was non-export of its system.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The sources do not show him discussing patriarchy; orthodox Marxism of his time subordinated it to class.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: He was part of the political elite and fell for abusing his office, so an adherent would reject the framing.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic limits on childbearing are not part of Yugoslav communist ideology and no source attributes them to him.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: His own security service was never held to account for killings and abuses in his lifetime; the Executive Committee charged only wiretapping and he was never prosecuted.

night-watchman-state.rationale: He led an expansive communist state apparatus.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Officially communist Yugoslavia opposed racialism, though his Kosovo policy favoured Serbs over Albanians.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Official ideology affirmed equality, though his Kosovo policy treated Albanians harshly; a weak yes.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Yugoslav communists built socialism in one country after the 1948 break with Stalin.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Settler colonialism as a concept is not discussed in the sources about him.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred from centralised uniform law and a secular outlook.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Conversion law is not discussed in the sources on him, so neutral.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Irrelevant to his setting; communists would not support it.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Communist Yugoslavia kept religion out of state schools.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: His fall was from a security state; he believed in strong state power, and the Stalin split heightened siege thinking.

consent-of-governed.rationale: His rule rested on party authority and police, not consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Trade balance targets are not discussed in the sources on his views.

population-transfer.rationale: The Kosovo article records Albanians and Muslim Slavs being pressed to declare themselves Turks and emigrate during his tenure; this is a documented practice attributed to him rather than a stated doctrine.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: His career as head of OZNA and UDBA involved purges and policing by force.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: A one-party regime that purged pro-Stalin communists would readily outlaw opponents.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Republican theories of liberty are not part of anything recorded about him.

separated-powers.rationale: His security service operated outside party control and he favoured concentrated authority.

vanguard-party.rationale: The League of Communists was the vanguard and he was one of its leading officials, favouring a centralised party-state.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Inferred from the egalitarian rhetoric of the League of Communists he served; undocumented for him personally.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Selling off state housing cuts against the state ownership he backed; inferred.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strikes were not legitimate in his party-state; inferred.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Marxist orthodoxy blames social institutions, not population, for poverty.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: His Kosovo policy suggests suspicion of minorities, but officially he stood for multinational unity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Filling offices by lottery is incompatible with the party appointments that ran his state.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: He kept a state of emergency in Kosovo until the mid-1960s, and the UDBA he led operated as a police state there.

party-controls-media.rationale: One-party state; his memoirs were later banned, and the party controlled the press.

party-commands-army.rationale: Leninist practice puts the army under party leadership, which is inferred for him as a party loyalist.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation rules are not discussed in the sources about him.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: The pay of representatives is not discussed in the sources on him.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Bešlin and Wikipedia depict him as orthodox on party discipline and democratic centralism.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: A centralist guarding the sovereignty of Yugoslavia.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The sources do not discuss presidential command versus legislative powers.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is not his concern; as a communist he wanted religious bodies weak and under state control.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rule by religious scholars is the opposite of the secular communist state he served and of his repression of Islam in Kosovo.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Lenin's slogan, but Yugoslav communists defended their country.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: A party-state with controlled culture would accept censorship, though his own reasons would be ideological rather than moral.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: His one-party state had no term limits on leaders such as Tito; inferred.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall by voters is not part of party-appointed rule; inferred and undocumented.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Yugoslavia stayed outside both blocs after 1948, which matches this position, though he never addressed it as such.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Compulsory home ownership is not a communist aim and is not discussed in sources on him.

people-in-arms.rationale: Yugoslavia had a professional army and territorial defence; inferred.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The sources record no view on rural versus urban life.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Reunification of divided nations is not addressed in the sources about him.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Anti-intellectual populism is not documented for him.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The sources record no position on cultural ranking.

death-penalty.rationale: Communist security chief of a state that executed political opponents after 1945.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Sex education is not addressed in the sources about him.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Teaching creationism conflicts with the secular, materialist education of communist Yugoslavia.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred from the conservative public morality of a 1950s communist security chief.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship law is not discussed in sources on him.

minority-language-support.rationale: Albanian-language institutions such as the University of Pristina were created only after his fall.

religious-exemptions.rationale: He repressed Islam in Kosovo; exemptions are opposed.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: A party loyalist demanding conformity would not encourage eccentric living; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Debt cancellation is not addressed in sources on him.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Marxist-Leninist view that formal independence needs socialist transformation; inferred.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The sources do not discuss how he would rewrite constitutions.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: A party-state that justified controls by building socialism fits this; inferred.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: International aid duties are not discussed in the sources on him.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons policy is not addressed in sources about him.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Head-of-state selection in his system went through the party; inferred.

central-bank-independence.rationale: A centralist who backed state direction of the economy would not give central banks independence from the government.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Land-for-peace deals are not addressed in the sources on him.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Socialist doctrine subordinates private property to social ownership, which he held as a communist.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: He fought pro-Stalin communists after 1948, yet an orthodox communist would not call the USSR capitalist.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental precaution did not arise in his time, so neutral.

collective-defense.rationale: Yugoslavia stayed outside NATO and the Warsaw Pact, and the sources do not address mutual defence.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Annexation law is not discussed in sources on him.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Kosovo account records his regime repressing Islam and the communist state curbing religious institutions.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Leninist leadership puts the head of state above all within the one party, not above party politics; inferred.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: He held that decentralisation threatened Yugoslav unity; his Kosovo policy treated Albanian autonomy as a security threat.

region-keeps-system.rationale: He opposed devolution of autonomy to regions.

sacred-ruler.rationale: A divine or sacred ruler is wholly foreign to Marxist-Leninist ideology and to his career as a communist.

flat-income-tax.rationale: A flat tax cuts against communist progressive-tax rhetoric; inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: Marxist doctrine holds that circumstances form character, which he held as a party official.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: His security service operated outside the law and party control, yet he was Tito's subordinate.

space-expansion.rationale: Space expansion as a civilizational aim is not addressed in sources on him.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Mixed-constitution theory has no place in a one-party Leninist state like the one he served.

leader-cult.rationale: He served Tito, whose cult was official, and did not challenge it.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody rules are not discussed in sources on him.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Purges after 1948 of alleged pro-Stalin communists suggest belief in internal enemies.

land-redistribution.rationale: The communist-led land reform of 1945 took large estates and gave them to farmers, which his party carried out.

refugee-return.rationale: His Kosovo policy pushed Albanians out and settled Serbs in their place.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Yugoslav communist policy did not claim territory abroad on ethnic grounds, though his Kosovo policy was nationalist in effect.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Punishing leaving a religion is contrary to communism, which promoted atheism, and contradicts the secular state he served.

women-must-cover.rationale: Compulsory covering contradicts the secular communist state, which discouraged religious dress.

common-currency.rationale: Currency union is not discussed in sources on him.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: He favoured Yugoslav unity, but unions of kin peoples across borders are not documented for him.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: He opposed Albanian autonomy and refused a Bosniak nationality.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The question of minority emigration versus equal rights is not addressed in the sources on him.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Historical materialism was the official doctrine of the League of Communists he served.

ban-cartels.rationale: Cartels did not arise in a state-planned economy, and the sources give no view.

no-bailouts.rationale: The state owned and directed enterprises, so the question has no clear application; no source speaks to it.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Inferred from a party-state in which courts were not independent checks on the ruling party.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Not addressed in any source on him; no basis for a position.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Not addressed; Yugoslavia traded with both blocs and the sources record no view.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Anachronistic question that the sources do not address.

moral-incentives.rationale: Yugoslav practice mixed material and moral incentives and no source records his stance.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: He was a Partisan leader in a guerrilla war, but the statement is about future revolutions and the sources give no view.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: A Partisan communist who fought for a republic that abolished the monarchy and titles.

history-own-civilization.rationale: History teaching is not addressed in the sources on him.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inferred from communist anti-colonial doctrine; nothing in sources.

patriotic-education.rationale: Yugoslav schools taught loyalty to the state and socialist Yugoslavia; inferred.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not addressed; the question does not fit his setting.

public-money-creation.rationale: Inferred from state control of the banking and credit system.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Marxist-Leninist orthodoxy holds that capitalism's crises are fundamental.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Not an aim of Yugoslav communist policy; inferred.

delink-world-market.rationale: Delinking from the world market is not addressed in sources on his views.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Labor aristocracy theory is not discussed in the sources on him.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: A state-centred communist would reject private freedom to discriminate.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Inferred from a party-state in which rights yielded to party authority.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial treaties are not addressed in sources on him.

elective-rulers.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; his party-state chose rulers by party selection.

minority-veto.rationale: Democratic centralism and his centralist stance mean decisions bind dissenters.

notes: Ranković left no systematic ideological writings, so the profile depends on documented policy and on how opponents and historians characterise it. Serbian historians dispute that he was a Serb nationalist, and Serbian public memory treats him as a defender of Serb interests while other republics link his name to repression.
